short: The City Dionysia festival in Athens saw the first recorded performance of tragedy, laying the foundation for Western theatre.
full:
In 534 BCE, the Athenian tyrant Peisistratos reorganised the City Dionysia, a festival dedicated to Dionysus, the god of wine and revelry. During this festival, the poet Thespis is said to have stepped out of the traditional chorus to speak individual lines, inventing the role of the actor and giving birth to Greek tragedy.

The festival grew into a massive civic event featuring dramatic competitions where playwrights submitted trilogies of tragedies followed by a satyr play. Held in the Theatre of Dionysus on the slopes of the Acropolis, these performances explored profound moral, religious, and political questions, becoming a vital part of Athenian democratic culture and establishing the dramatic forms still used today.
